spans.s:
नभ् 1. नभ्, cl. 1. A. नभते, &c., Ved.
to burst, to be torn or rent asunder; to
hurt, injure, destroy, (नेभे occurs in Bhaṭṭi-kāvya
XIV. 33

2. नभ्, प्, f., Ved. (according to Sāy.) hurt,
injury, destruction.

नाभ् नाभ्, प्, f. (fr. rt. 1. नभ्), Ved.
an opening, aperture, mouth (?); a rent (?); (Sāy.)
destructive, obstructing.

नभनु, उस्, m. and ऊ, ऊस्, f., Ved. a spring,
river, (water which bursts forth.)

1. नभन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नभन), Ved. burst-
ing out, breaking or coming forth (as a hymn or as
a horse). According to Sāy. = ‘being in the sky,’
[]
‘ethereal;’ ‘injuring,’ ‘destroying;’ ‘a hymn.’ (For
2. नभन्य see under नभ below.)

2. नभन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy.)
being in the sky, ethereal, heavenly; (see col. 2.)

नभन्व, अस्, m., Ved. a river; (according to
modern scholars the form is नभनु.)

नभ नभ, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. नह्
with affix भ, but rather fr. नभ् an older form of
1. नह्, ‘to bind,’ ‘connect,’ as ‘connecting heaven
and earth;’ according to others fr. rt. 1. नभ्, ‘to
rend asunder or be broken up into clouds’), = नभस्,
the sky, atmosphere; the month Śrāvaṇa (July —
August); N. of a son of Manu Svārociṣa or of the
third Manu (mentioned together with Nabhasya);
N. of one of the seven sages of the sixth Manv-
antara; N. of a demon, son of Vipra-citti by Siṃhikā;
N. of a son of Nala (Niṣadha) and father of Puṇ-
ḍarīka [cf. नभस्]; (आ), f. a spitting-pot (for
नभास्?); N. of the city of the Sun; [cf. Zend
nap-ta, ‘moist, wet;’ Gr. νέφ-ος, νεφ-έλη, ξυν-νέ-νοφε,
νεφό-ω, probably δνόφος, ἰο-δνέφής,
γνό-φος; Lat. nūb-ē-s, nūbilu-s, nēbula, probably Nep-
tū-nu-s, nimbu-s for nembu-s; Old Iceland. nifl-
heim-r; Old Germ. nib-ul; Mod. Germ. neb-el;
Angl. Sax. ge-nip, ‘a cloud;’ Slav. neb-o, base neb-
es, ‘sky;’ Lith. debes-i-s, ‘a cloud,’ through change
of n into d, as in dewyni, ‘nine;’ Hib. neamh,
‘heaven;’ Cambro-Brit. nev, ‘heaven.’]
—नभ-
ग, अस्, m. ‘going on the sky,’ N. of a son of Manu
Vaivasvata; [cf. नभाग, नाभाग.]
नाभ नाभ. See p. 478, col. 1.

नाभ (substituted for नाभि at the end of an
adj. comp.), the navel (e. g. अब्ज-नाभ, अस्, m.
‘lotus-naveled,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu; cf. उन्-न्˚,
ऊर्ण-न्˚, कञ्ज-न्˚, काल-न्˚); the nave of a
wheel; the centre or central point of anything;
(अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; N. of a son of Śruta
and father of Sindhu-dvīpa.

नभस्, अस्, n. fog, vapour; a cloud; sky, atmo-
sphere, ether or heaven; ether as one of the five ele-
ments; N. of a month in the rainy season (= श्रा-
वण) or July-August, (according to lexicographers in
this sense m.); period of life, age; the vapour or
fluidity of the Soma (Ved.); water (Ved.); the sun
(according to Nir.
II. 14

); (आस्), m. a cloud, the
rains or the rainy season; the nose, smell; the fibres
in the root of a lotus or a rope made of lotus fibres;
a spitting-pot; N. of a prince, son of Nala and father
of Puṇḍarīka; (असी), n. du. both worlds, heaven and
earth.
—नभः-केतन, अम्, n. ‘sky-banner,’ the
sun.
—नभः-क्रान्त, अस्, or नभः-क्रान्तिन्, ई,
m. ‘going in the sky’ (from the lion-like shape
of certain clouds), a lion.
—नभः-पान्थ, अस्,
m. ‘sky-traveller,’ the sun.
—नभः-प्रभेद,
अस्, m., N. of a descendant of Vi-rūpa and author of
a Ṛg-veda hymn (

).
—नभः-प्राण, अस्,
m. ‘sky-breath,’ air, wind; [cf. ख-श्वास, नभः-
श्वास.]
—नभः-श्रित्, त्, त्, त्, reaching to the sky,
attaining heaven.
—नभः-श्वास, अस्, m. ‘sky-
breath,’ air, wind; [cf. नभः-प्राण.]
—नभः-
सद्, त्, m. ‘inhabiting the sky,’ a god; a star.
—नभः-सरस्, अस्, n. ‘sky-lake,’ the clouds.
—नभः-सरित्, f. ‘sky-river,’ the milky-way (=
देव-पथ); the celestial Ganges.
—नभः-स्थ,
अस्, आ, अम्, ‘situated in heaven,’ celestial, aerial,
heavenly, ethereal.
—नभः-स्थल, अस्, m. ‘whose
residence is the sky,’ an epithet of Śiva; (ई), f. the
sky.
—नभः-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, abiding in heaven
or in the sky; (अस्), m. a division of the infernal
regions, a hell.
—नभः-स्पृश्, क्, क्, क्, or नभः-
स्पृश, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘sky-touching,’ reaching to
the sky.
—नभश्-चक्षुस्, उस्, m. ‘eye of the
sky,’ the sun.
—नभश्-चमस, अस्, m. ‘drinking
vessel of heaven,’ the moon; a variegated cake (=
चित्र-पूप); magic, conjuring.
—नभश्-चर, अस्,
ई, अम्, ‘sky-going,’ going in the air; (अस्), m. an
inhabitant of heaven, a god; a Vidyā-dhara or demi-
god so called.
—नभस्-तल, अम्, n. ‘the bottom
of the clouds,’ the lower region of the sky, nether
sky; the sky, atmosphere; (in astronomy) N. of the
tenth solar mansion.
—नभस्-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
Ved. vaporous, vapory, filled with vapour, exhaling
vapour, misty, hazy; (Sāy.) bright as the sun.
 — 1. नभस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, vaporous, filled with
vapour, misty, cloudy; young; (आन्), m. air, wind;
(अती), f., N. of the wife of Antar-dhāna and mother
of Havir-dhāna.
—२. नभस्-वत्, ind. like vapour.
—नभो-ग, अस्, अम्, m. n. (?), a star; (अस्), m.,
[]
N. of one of the seven sages of the tenth Manv-
antara.
—नभो-गज, अस्, m. ‘an elephant in the
sky,’ a cloud.
—नभो-गति, इस्, f. going through
the sky, going in the air, soaring, flying.
—नभो-
जा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. produced from vapour.
—नभो-
जू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, Ved. impelling the clouds; (Sāy.)
pervading or traversing the sky.
—नभो-द, अस्,
m., N. of one of the Viśve-devās.
—नभो-दुह,
‘milking the sky;’ or नभो-द्वीप, ‘sky-island;’ or
नभो-धूम, ‘sky-smoke;’ or नभो-ध्वज, अस्,
m. ‘sky-banner,’ a cloud.
—नभो-दृष्टि, इस्, इस्,
इ, blind; looking up to heaven.
—नभो-नदी, f.
‘sky-river,’ the celestial Ganges.
—नभो-मणि, इस्,
m. ‘sky-jewel,’ the sun.
—नभो-मण्डल, अम्,
n. ‘sky-circle,’ the firmament; the atmosphere.
—नभोमण्डल-दीप, अस्, m. ‘light of the sky,’
the moon.
—नभो ऽम्बु-प, अस्, m. ‘drinking the
water of the sky or rain-water,’ the bird Cātaka,
Cuculus Melanoleucus.
—नभो-योनि, इस्, m. ‘whose
birthplace is the sky,’ epithet of Śiva.
—नभो-
रजस्, अस्, n. ‘sky-dust (?),’ darkness.
—नभो-रूप,
अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having the form or colour of the
clouds, dark-coloured.
—नभो-रेणु, उस्, f. fog,
mist, vapour.
—नभो-लय, अस्, m. ‘having its
abode in the sky,’ smoke.
—नभो-लिह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, ‘sky-
licking,’ lofty, towering, rising to the clouds.
—नभो-
वट, अस्, m. ‘the expanse of the sky,’ the atmo-
sphere.
—नभो-विद्, त्, त्, त्, knowing or possessing
heaven or the sky.
—नभो-वीथी, f. ‘sky-road,’ the
path of the sun.
—नभौकस् (नभ for नभस्
+ ओकस्), inhabiting the atmosphere or heaven.

नभस, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. vapourish, vapoury,
filled with vapour, misty; (अस्), m. heaven, air,
atmosphere; the rainy season; the ocean; N. of
one of the seven sages in the tenth Manv-antara; of
a Dānava; (also read रभस.)
—नभसङ्-
गम, अस्, m. ‘sky-goer,’ a bird.

नाभस नाभस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नभस्),
celestial, heavenly, appearing in the sky; (with
योग) N. of certain constellations, (according to
Bhaṭṭotpala there are thirty-two, divided into four
classes, viz. three Āśraya-yogas, two Dala-yogas,
twenty Ākṛti-yogas, and seven Saṅkhyā-yogas.)
—नाभस-योगाध्याय (˚ग-अध्˚), अस्, m., N.
of the twelfth chapter of the Bṛhaj-jātaka, an astro-
logical work by Varāha-mihira.

नभस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, vapoury, filled with vapour,
misty, foggy; (अस्), m., N. of a month of the rainy
season (= Bhādra, August-September); N. of a son
of Manu Svārociṣa or of the third Manu [cf. नभ];
epithet of Śiva.

नभाक, अस्, m., N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi by whom
three hymns of the Ṛg-veda (
VIII. 39
VIII. 40

= the
hymn of Nabhāka.

नाभक नाभक, अस्, m. a myrobalan, Ter-
minalia Chebula.

नाभाक नाभाक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नभाक),
belonging to or composed by Nabhāka; (अस्), m. (like
नभाक), Ved., N. of a Ṛṣi of the Kaṇva family.
1. नभ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, foggy, misty, cloudy.

नभ्य 2. नभ्य, अम्, n. (said to be fr. नभ
for नाभि), Ved. the centre part of a wheel, the
nave; the middle.
—नभ्य-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्,
standing in the middle; belonging to the nave of
a wheel, fit for a nave; नभ्यं तैलम्, oil for
greasing the nave of a wheel.

नाभ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, proceeding from the navel,
being in the navel, umbilical, of or relating to
the navel; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; [cf.
नाभ.]

नभाग नभाग, अस्, m., N. of a son of
Manu Vaivasvata; [cf. नभ-ग, नाभाग.]

नाभाग नाभाग, अस्, m. (fr. नभ-ग), N.
of a son of Manu Vaivasvata; a patronymic of Am-
barīṣa [cf. नाभागि]; a son of Manu and father of
Ambarīṣa, &c.; a son of Nabha-ga or Nabhāga and
father of Ambarīṣa; a son of Śruta and father of
Ambarīṣa; of a son of Nediṣṭha or Ariṣṭa or
Diṣṭa and father of Bhalandana; of a son of Yayāti,
grandson of Ambarīṣa, and father of Aja; [cf.
नभाग, नाभा-नेदिष्ठ.]
—नाभाग-दिष्ट,
अस्, m., N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata; [cf. ना-
भा-नेदिष्ठ, नाभाग, दिष्ट.]
—नाभाग-
धेय, perhaps = नाभाग-भागधेय, one who
has the same lot or destiny as Nābhāga.
—नाभाग-
नेदिष्ठ, अस्, m. and नाभागारिष्ट (˚ग-अर्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata; [cf. नाभाग,
अरिष्ट.]
नभि नभि, इस्, m. (?), a wheel.

नाभि नाभि, इस्, or नाभी, f. (according to
[]
lexicographers also m.; probably fr. नभ्, an older
form of rt. 1. नह्, to bind, connect), the navel;
any navel-like cavity; the nave of a wheel (e. g.
त्रि-नाभि चक्रम्, a three-naved wheel, a wheel
with a triple nave or centre, Ṛg-veda
XVIII. 19

= the chief of the circle of kings); the
close connection of relations, near relationship, com-
munity of race or family; home; a near relation;
musk (= मृग-नाभि); (इस्), m. a sovereign, a
lord paramount; a chief; a Kṣatriya or Hindū of
the regal and military tribe; N. of a grandson of
Priya-vrata [cf. नाभि-गुप्त, नाभि-वर्ष], son
of Agnīdhra and father of Ṛṣabha; of the father of
Ṛṣabha, first Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; [cf.
नाभ, 2. नभ्य, अन्य-न्˚, घन-न्˚, &c.: cf.
also Gr. ὀμφ-αλό-ς, ὅμφαξ: Lat. umb-il-īcu-s,
umbo: Old Germ. nab-a, ‘nave;’ nabulo, ‘navel:’
Angl. Sax. nafu, nafela: Mod. Germ. nabe, na-
bel: Lett. nabba, ‘navel:’ Lith. namba, ‘navel.’]
—नाभा-नेदिष्ठ, अस्, m. (नाभा loc. sing. for
नाभौ), N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata and
author of two Ṛg-veda hymns, (Ṛg-veda

.)
—नाभानेदिष्ठ, अस्, ई, अम्, or नाभाने-
धिष्ठीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or composed by
Nābhā-nediṣṭha; (अम्), n., scil. सूक्तम्, N. of a
Vedic hymn.
—नाभि-कण्टक, अस्, m. ruptured or
protruded navel (= commonly गोण्ड).
—नाभि-गु-
डक, अस्, m. a protruding or ruptured navel.
—ना-
भि-गुप्त, अस्, m. (?), ‘protected by Nābhi,’ N. of
a Varṣa in Kuśa-dvīpa, (the king of Kuśa-dvīpa was
Hiraṇya-retas, a son of Priya-vrata, who divided the
seven Varṣas of his Dvīpa among his seven sons;
Nābhi was probably the N. of one of these seven
sons; cf. नाभि-वर्ष.)
—नाभि-गोलक, अस्, m.
a protruding or ruptured navel (= नाभि-गुडक).
—नाभि-च्छेदन, अम्, n. cutting or separating
the umbilical cord.
—नाभि-ज, अस्, m. or नाभि-
जन्मन्, आ, m. an epithet of Brahmā, (this deity
appearing on the lotus which sprang from the navel
of Viṣṇu.)
—नाभि-द्वार, अम्, n. the aperture
of the navel.
—नाभि-नाडी, f. or नाभि-नाला, f. or
नाभि-नाल, अम्, n. the umbilical cord; [cf. गर्-
भ-नाडी.]
—नाभि-भू, ऊस्, m. ‘born from the
navel,’ an epithet of Brahmā; [cf. नाभि-ज.]
—ना-
भि-मूल, अम्, n. the part of the body immediately
under the navel.
—नाभि-वर्धन, अम्, n. division
of the umbilical cord; rupture of the navel, umbilical
hernia; corpulency.
—नाभि-वर्ष, अस्, अम्, m. n.
the Varṣa governed by Nābhi, son of Āgnīdhra (=
भारत-वर्ष).
—नाभ्य्-आवर्त, अस्, m. the cavity
of the navel.

नभीत न-भीत, अस्, आ, अम्, not afraid, un-
daunted, dauntless.
—नभीत-वत्, ind. in a fearless
manner, fearlessly.

नभ्राज् न-भ्राज्, ट्, m. ‘not shining,’ a
dark cloud.
नाभागि, इस्, m. a patronymic of Ambarīṣa.

नाभिक, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of an adj. comp.)
= नाभि (e. g. षण्-णाभिक, having six naves);
(आ), f. a cavity shaped like a navel; a species of
plant, Achyranthes Atropurpurea (= कटभी).
—ना-
भिक-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town of the Uttara-
kurus.

नाभिल, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to or coming from
a navel; [cf. नाभील.]

नाभील, अम्, n. the groin of a woman; a promi-
nent or ruptured navel; the cavity of the navel; pain.

नाभेय, अस्, m. a patronymic of Ṛṣabha, first
Arhat of the Jainas.

नाभिजात नाभिजात (न-अभिजात), अस्, आ,
अम्, not well-born, not noble, low-bred, ignoble.

नाभिमान नाभिमान (न-अभ्˚), अस्, m. ab-
sence of pride, humbleness.
